core_concepts_formalized: Poisson point process (PPP) and independent thinning as conditions for binned Poisson approximations; cascade multi-photon emission introduces cross-bin event correlation requiring dedicated event-level or coincidence modeling
Full joint likelihood combines discrete Poisson binned counting with continuous joint auxiliary calibration constraints p_aux(a | nu)
Distinction between population theoretical variance Var(S) = mu_P + a^2 mu_R and sample plug-in estimate widehat{Var}(S) = P + a^2 R
First-order Taylor expansion V_y approx J V_x J^T requires only uncorrelatedness for cross-terms to vanish; uncorrelatedness is strictly weaker than statistical independence
Branching ratio normalization sum b_k = 1 imposes a linear row-sum constraint sum_j Cov(b_i, b_j) = 0; pair covariances are universally negative only under a specific multinomial distribution

Raw fitted peak area covariance V_A arises from spectrum deconvolution, while efficiency-corrected yield covariance V_I inherits shared calibration parameters that can produce positive or negative cross-energy covariance
Dimensionless live-time fraction LT in (0, 1] and independence factorization assumptions; coincidence joint acceptance does not automatically factorize into scalar products

Wilks theorem degrees of freedom equal the dimension of tested interest parameters (dim(theta)), excluding profiled nuisance parameters; profile curvature distinguishes -ln L Hessian (cov approx H_1^-1) from -2ln L Hessian (cov approx 2 H_2^-1)

Physical boundary constraints: profile likelihood on mu >= 0 rescales the reference likelihood denominator with constrained MLE hat{mu}_phys = 0 (yielding q_phys(mu) = mu^2 - 2 hat{mu} mu for Gaussian), without falsely shifting the observational data center hat{mu}

Feldman-Cousins unified approach is an exact Neyman acceptance-band construction based on likelihood-ratio ordering, exhibiting step-like over-coverage for discrete Poisson counts; Delta chi^2 = 2.71 is merely an illustrative asymptotic 1-sided Gaussian benchmark

Monte Carlo pushforward distributions represent measurement error propagation under functional mapping; they constitute Bayesian posteriors if and only if input samples derive from genuine conditional posterior probability laws under explicit priors
